items.name: narration_en
items.direction: Narrate this for a premium documentary YouTube Shorts channel about money, history and the tricks behind them. The Narrator is a deep, warm, confident storyteller with a hint of mystery: curious, quietly amused, energetic and punchy, never slow, never announcer-like. Natural emphasis on dates and numbers, questions end with a curious lift, a short comic pause before each punchline. Keep the same voice, pace and energy from start to finish.
lines: Narrator
That hundred dollar ticket becomes a hundred and thirty at checkout. That's no accident.
Narrator
It's called drip pricing: the fees drip in at the very end.
Narrator
In a StubHub experiment with millions of users, hiding fees until checkout made people spend about twenty-one percent more.
Narrator
And they were about fourteen percent more likely to buy at all.
Narrator
Why? By checkout, you've picked your seats. They already feel like yours.
Narrator
So in May twenty twenty-five, a US rule made ticket sellers and hotels show the full price up front.
Narrator
Taxes can still come later. But mandatory fees? No more surprises.
Narrator
That's the mirage: the price you see first isn't the price. It's the bait.
Narrator
So judge every deal by the total at checkout, not the number that hooked you.
Narrator
This is Money Mirage. Follow for more.
